name: Intelligent Payment Routing
tagline: Build a routing policy that generalises beyond the visible case.
narrative:
You are joining YamusaPay's Payments Infrastructure team. The switch receives consumer, business, refund, and international payments while provider health changes in real time.

Each route consumes provider capacity until processing finishes. A failed payment may be retried, but retries consume time, capacity, and cost. The visible stream teaches the contract; Submit tests the same policy against unseen outages, capacity limits, fee changes, latency spikes, and high-value traffic.
objective: Process the visible stream without timeouts, protect urgent payments, and submit a policy that works across the hidden scenarios.
learningObjective: Combine eligibility, capacity, reliability, urgency, cost, and retry history in one ordered policy.
intelligenceExplanation:
The interview starts with an empty rule set. Build the decision flow from the operational facts.

Filter providers that cannot accept the current payment first. Only then compare reliability, deadline risk, queue pressure, and cost. Being online does not guarantee that a provider is eligible for every payment.
hint: Start with `canRoute`, deadline, payment type, amount, and retry history. Compare cost only after unsafe options are removed.
hints: Separate eligibility from preference. Use canRouteA/B/C before fee or expected cost.
Reserve the most reliable, low-latency route for urgent or high-value payments, and avoid immediately repeating a failed provider.
A robust fallback ends in hold only when the deadline permits waiting; otherwise choose an eligible route or decline deliberately.
brief: Author and submit a resilient payment policy for changing provider conditions.
context: Each tick makes one routing decision while providers continue processing earlier payments in parallel.
